H1.title: Phylogeny-Conditional Per-Genome Dark Fraction vs Nearest-Relative AAI and RBH Coverage in Desert Thermoplasmatota
H1.execution_status: COMPLETE (Slurm job 53704703 on IBEX, 00:00:42, exit 0:0; 67/67 SHA-256 checksums verified in h1_final; full finite cohort n = 237 dereplicated desert Thermoplasmatota species representatives across 7 PGLS specifications S1-S7; retained statsmodels.GLS verification in v3_pgls_statsmodels_verification.tsv agrees to <= 5.16e-12 on beta, <= 3.15e-13 on SE, <= 4.44e-15 on R^2_GLS; major transcription error in h2_initial/H1_COMPLETENESS.md resolved in h2_v2/H1_COMPLETENESS.md)
H1.main_vs_supplement: Main text: 2-3 sentences in the Thermoplasmatota subsection (manuscript/main.tex lines 252-306) stating that across the 237 dereplicated Thermoplasmatota species representatives on the 1,914-tip GTDB-Tk r232 ar53 tree, per-genome dark fraction shows strong residual phylogenetic covariance under Pagel's lambda PGLS (lambda_ML = 0.915784, 95% profile-likelihood CI [0.846303, 0.957823], LRT vs lambda = 0: 2 Delta ell = 229.5585, p = 7.44e-52; R^2_GLS = 0.469051) and that conditioned on phylogeny and assembly quality covariates, nearest-relative AAI (+0.001704 +/- 0.000407, p = 4.07e-5) and RBH coverage (-0.137484 +/- 0.019456, p = 1.88e-11) exhibit opposite-signed partial associations. Supplement: full 7-model specification table (S1-S7), lambda profile-likelihood grid, comparator metadata summary (32 unique GTDB/MGnify reference accessions), and dual gene-caller reconciliation.
supported_claims: Across all n = 237 dereplicated Rub' al-Khali Thermoplasmatota species representatives (185 c__SW-10-69-26, 51 c__E2, 1 c__Thermoplasmata) on the 1,914-tip GTDB-Tk r232 ar53 tree, per-genome dark fraction (N_dark / N_proteins_cat) exhibits strong residual phylogenetic covariance under Pagel's lambda PGLS (lambda_ML = 0.915784, 95% profile-likelihood CI [0.846303, 0.957823], LRT against OLS lambda = 0: 2 Delta ell = 229.5585, p = 7.4411e-52; R^2_GLS = 0.469051, OLS R^2 = 0.495786).

In the primary PGLS model (S1_Primary_All_237, n = 237, p = 7, df = 230) controlling for CheckM2 completeness (beta = -0.000335 +/- 0.000126, p = 8.398044e-3), contamination (beta = -0.000320 +/- 0.000491, p = 5.159032e-1), log10 genome length (beta = +0.115427 +/- 0.018391, p = 1.706357e-9), and log10 N50 (beta = -0.009005 +/- 0.003031, p = 3.284365e-3), dark fraction has a positive partial association with nearest-relative AAI (beta_AAI = +0.001704 +/- 0.000407, t = +4.1847, two-sided p = 4.065008e-5, conditional 95% t-CI [+0.000902, +0.002506]; union across the 95% profile-likelihood lambda CI is [+0.000758, +0.002550]) and a negative partial association with RBH coverage (beta_RBH = -0.137484 +/- 0.019456, t = -7.0664, two-sided p = 1.879206e-11, conditional 95% t-CI [-0.175819, -0.099149]; union across the 95% profile-likelihood lambda CI is [-0.178736, -0.095753]).

Both conditional partial associations retain the same sign and statistical significance across all six sensitivity specifications in v3_pgls_sensitivity.tsv: S2 unnormalized Brownian VCV (n = 237, beta_AAI = +0.001744 +/- 0.000407, p = 2.694748e-5; beta_RBH = -0.140505 +/- 0.019533, p = 8.831619e-12), S3 shared catalogue denominator for RBH (n = 237, beta_AAI = +0.001693 +/- 0.000407, p = 4.499514e-5; beta_RBH = -0.136591 +/- 0.019416, p = 2.265112e-11), S4 restricted to c__SW-10-69-26 (n = 185, beta_AAI = +0.001921 +/- 0.000491, p = 1.285632e-4; beta_RBH = -0.180441 +/- 0.022624, p = 1.776834e-13), S5 omitting dominant family f__JAJPHT01 (n = 97, beta_AAI = +0.001494 +/- 0.000513, p = 4.526286e-3; beta_RBH = -0.102379 +/- 0.030547, p = 1.176333e-3), S6 same-class comparators in c__SW-10-69-26 and c__E2 (n = 236, beta_AAI = +0.001568 +/- 0.000392, p = 8.387793e-5; beta_RBH = -0.145879 +/- 0.019191, p = 7.485088e-13), and S7 complete-gene proxy adding CheckM2 frac_complete (n = 232, beta_AAI = +0.001550 +/- 0.000452, p = 7.245799e-4; beta_RBH = -0.104756 +/- 0.026891, p = 1.293680e-4).
prohibited_claims: Do not interpret Pagel's lambda = 0.915784 as a percentage of variance explained in darkness or as proof that vertical lineage history dominates all other explanations; describe it strictly as residual phylogenetic covariance under the fitted PGLS model.

Do not interpret the positive partial slope on AAI as a positive marginal relationship, and do not describe N_dark and N_RBH as disjoint core-versus-accessory proteome partitions (they derive from different gene callers and non-mutually-exclusive criteria, since external GTDB/MGnify reference MAGs also contain unannotated proteins).

Do not claim that the H1 associations demonstrate accessory genome expansion, ancestral gene gain/loss polarity, horizontal gene transfer, de novo gene birth, cultivation-status effects, or an explanation of between-phylum darkness differences.

Do not describe the 32 unique external reference comparators (229 pairs to GTDB r232 species representatives and 8 pairs to MGnify genomes; 142 soil, 3 marine sediment, 92 GTDB-only without habitat metadata) as cultivated isolates, or present 237 pair counts as 237 unique comparator genomes.

Do not present Student-t intervals and p-values as random-sampling inferences over a larger population; the 237 genomes are the enumerated study cohort, and intervals are model-based and conditional on the fixed FastTree topology/branch lengths and fitted lambda.

Do not use the superseded hand-transcribed table in reviews/darkmatter-2026-10-13/round7/snapshots/h2_initial/H1_COMPLETENESS.md (Section 4); use only h1_final/results/v3_pgls_model_summary.tsv and the regenerated h2_v2/H1_COMPLETENESS.md.

H2.title: Flanking Gene-Neighbourhood KO Recurrence Across Multi-Species Structural Dark Families: Low-Query-TM (K) vs Fold-Matched (QnotK)
H2.execution_status: COMPLETE (Slurm job 53738443 on IBEX, 00:05:21, exit 0:0; 26/26 snapshot files and 13/13 output SHA-256 checksums verified; full Gate 3 census of 1,461 multi-species families [570 low-query-TM K with qTM < 0.5; 891 fold-matched QnotK with qTM >= 0.5] and 7,604 member rows across 2,126 refined bins audited)
H2.main_vs_supplement: Main text: 1-2 sentences in the structural subsection (manuscript/main.tex lines 307-351) reporting that among the 353 multi-species families evaluable under complete 4-flank exact-coordinate Bakta windows (173/570 = 30.35% in low-query-TM K, 180/891 = 20.20% in fold-matched QnotK), flanking KO recurrence exceeds same-contig eligible-position expectations within both arms (40.46% vs 8.71% in K, p = 0.0002; 32.22% vs 6.56% in QnotK, p = 0.0002), whereas the between-arm difference is null once conditioned on species breadth, coarse host phylum group, and flanking KO annotation opportunity (Delta_MH(E_fam) = +0.035358, p = 0.4069; strict 96-pair matched raw difference 0.0000, p = 1.0000; OLS/HC3 beta_is_k = +0.029446 +/- 0.042950, p = 0.4930). Supplement: full 2,838 -> 1,461 -> 353 (Tier 1) / 637 (Tier 2) / 1,320 (Tier 3) attrition funnel, 7-category flank coordinate audit, 16-stratum common-support table, caliper matching diagnostics, regression tables, and cross-family dependence bounds.
supported_claims: Across the 2,838 confidence-qualified (mean pLDDT >= 0.70, length >= 100 aa, monomer) structural dark families (1,031 low-query-TM K with qTM < 0.5 against PDB and AFDB; 1,807 fold-matched QnotK with qTM >= 0.5), 1,461 families (51.48%: 570 K, 891 QnotK) span >= 2 distinct dRep 95% ANI species clusters at Gate 3 (7,604 candidate member rows; 4,542 designated primary species-representative loci across 2,126 refined bins, of which 2,041/2,126 = 96.00% pass exact uppercase contig SHA-256 and Bakta .log orig-id verification with zero hash or reverse-complement mismatches).

Under the primary Tier 1 complete-window gate (>= 2 species whose primary locus has all 4 flanks m2, m1, p1, p2 present on the contig and mapped by exact coordinates to Bakta/eggNOG; n = 353 evaluable families: 173 K, 180 QnotK; 1,380 Tier 1 eligible primary loci across all 1,461 families and 877 across the 353 evaluable families), flanking KO recurrence is enriched above same-contig eligible-position expectations (B = 5,000 draws) within both K (40.4624% [70/173] observed vs 8.7114% expected; within-arm excess +31.7510 percentage points, p = 0.0002) and QnotK (32.2222% [58/180] observed vs 6.5551% expected; within-arm excess +25.6671 percentage points, p = 0.0002).

Between arms, low-query-TM families (K) do not differ significantly from fold-matched families (QnotK) in neighborhood KO recurrence once conditioned on species breadth, coarse host phylum group, and flanking KO annotation opportunity: in Tier 1 (n = 353, 16/16 common-support strata, 100% coverage), Delta_MH(E_fam) = +0.035358 (null SD 0.042346, p = 0.406859) and Delta_MH(C_fam) = +0.053850 (null SD 0.046674, p = 0.259774); in Tier 2 (3'-stop sensitivity, n = 637: 260 K, 377 QnotK, 16/16 strata), Delta_MH(E_fam) = +0.018391 (null SD 0.031223, p = 0.561844) and Delta_MH(C_fam) = +0.043859 (null SD 0.034337, p = 0.232277); in strict 1:1 exact-phylum and tight-length caliper matching (96 pairs), raw recurrence is 31.25% in both arms (Delta = 0.0000, p = 1.0000) and excess difference is -0.005440 (p = 0.922608); in multivariable OLS/HC3 (n = 353), beta_is_k = +0.029446 +/- 0.042950 (p = 0.492970) on E_fam and +0.049661 +/- 0.046674 (p = 0.287330) on raw C_fam; in MLE logistic regression, beta_is_k = +0.280149 +/- 0.296352 (OR = 1.323327, p = 0.344492).
prohibited_claims: Do not invert the definitions of K and QnotK or label either arm as proven novel folds: K is the low-whole-query-TM group (qTM < 0.5 against PDB and AFDB) and QnotK is the fold-matched sequence-dark comparator group (qTM >= 0.5).
Do not claim that low-query-TM families (K) have higher genomic neighborhood conservation than fold-matched families (QnotK).

Do not claim that the 11-keyword mobilome screen on the single top recurrent KO (best_ko_mobilome_flag == 0 across 128 recurrent families) establishes conserved 'non-mobilome' genomic neighborhoods or excludes mobile genetic elements, prophages, or plasmids (62.68% [3,460/5,520] of Tier 1 flanks have no KO assignment, mapped_noKO).

Do not cite the unadjusted Tier 3 partial-window comparison (33.5893% [175/521] in K vs 24.6558% [197/799] in QnotK, raw difference +0.089334, Fisher p = 0.000458 across n = 1,320 families with >= 1 mapped flank) as evidence of higher syntenic conservation in K; Tier 3 lacks a same-contig positional reference and is confounded by unequal numbers of exact-mapped flanks per locus (mean 2.80 in K vs 2.71 in QnotK) and higher partial-window species counts in K (mean 3.22 vs 2.91).

Do not extrapolate Tier 1 recurrence rates (40.46% in K, 32.22% in QnotK) as unconditional population rates for all 2,838 structural dark families or all 1,461 multi-species families without reporting the 75.84% (1,108/1,461) complete-window attrition and differential Tier 1 survival (30.35% in K vs 20.20% in QnotK, two-sided Fisher p = 1.46e-5).

major_findings.title: High and differential complete-window attrition in Tier 1 (30.35% K vs 20.20% QnotK, p = 1.46e-5) and unadjusted partial-window confounding in Tier 3
major_findings.evidence: reviews/darkmatter-2026-10-13/round7/snapshots/h2_v2/results/pilot_family_conservation.tsv, pilot_neighbourhoods.tsv, and pilot_conservation_summary.json (verified in verify_h1_h2_facts.json). Only 353/1,461 (24.16%) Gate 3 families pass Tier 1 (173/570 = 30.35% in K vs 180/891 = 20.20% in QnotK, two-sided Fisher exact p = 1.4587e-5), whereas in Tier 2 (n = 637, 43.60%) per-locus eligibility equalizes (49.73% vs 49.44%) and Delta_MH(E_fam) = +0.018391 (p = 0.561844), Delta_MH(C_fam) = +0.043859 (p = 0.232277). Tier 3 (n = 1,320) computes no positional null or stratified contrast and divides ko_annotation_opportunity_partial by t3_callable_flanks rather than 4 * n_sp_t3.
